frames.narration: 02:00. The primary holds about 1.20 million orders. A base backup copies the data files (500 GB) and records the log position it started at.
All day, finished log segments are copied to the archive, and a timeout ships a partial segment every 5 minutes. The archive plus the base backup is a complete history.
The replica applies the same log within about a second, so it is a live copy for failover. That is its only job here.
14:03. Someone runs DELETE FROM orders with no WHERE. The primary now has 0 of its 1.23 million orders, and the delete is just another log record.
One second later the replica has applied it too: 0 orders. Replication copied the mistake, so failing over would not bring the data back.
14:08. The operator notices, stops writes and picks the target 14:02:59, one second before the DELETE. The newest base backup before it is the 02:00 one.
Step 1: copy the 500 GB base backup into a fresh instance. At about 200 MB/s that is roughly 43 minutes, and it grows with data size.
Step 2: replay 12 hours of archived log, about 434 GB at 600 MB/min, at roughly 50 MB/s. That is about 2 h 25 min, and it stops at 14:02:59.

Done after about 3 hours: 1.23 million orders are back and only 1 second of work is lost (RPO). The operator checks counts, then copies the table back or promotes this instance. Restoring to 14:03:01 instead would replay the DELETE.
